Real Estate Automation System: From First Form to Follow-Up

One connected system for a real estate agency, built as a portfolio project. It takes a lead from the first form fill to a booked, AI-summarised, property-matched discovery call, then follows up after the call and handles the back-office paperwork, with nobody copying data between tabs.

GoHighLeveln8nMake.comGroq AIGoogle SheetsCal.comFathomAsanaXero

Estimates, not measured client data. This is a portfolio build for a mock real estate agency. The monthly volumes beside each row are sample numbers. Manual times are typical handling for an agent or VA; the automated figure is the review time that remains.

01 The problem

Leads arrived from web forms and Facebook, then waited for someone to sort them, tag them, send the right questionnaire, hunt for listings and chase the discovery call. Slow replies cost deals, the same data was retyped across three tools, and nothing happened after the call unless someone remembered.

02 The build

One front-door form routes every lead by type in GoHighLevel. n8n and a Groq AI agent summarise and categorise answers and fetch matching listings. The discovery-call, after-call, nurture and invoicing workflows keep every later step in sync.

03 The result

Every lead is tagged, assigned and followed up within a minute. The agent opens a contact that already has a summary, a category and a shortlist of properties, and spends the time on the call instead of the admin.

What the agency needed
  • Reply fast. Every new lead gets the right message within a minute, whatever the time of day.
  • Route correctly. Buyers, sellers and mixed enquiries reach the right agent, pipeline and task without anyone sorting by hand.
  • Arrive prepared. Each call starts with a summary, a category and, for buyers, a property shortlist.
  • Never go quiet. Bookings, reschedules, cancellations and post-call outcomes each trigger the next step.
  • Keep the books in step. Finished work flows into invoicing without retyping.

2 workflows

Built to be safe and easy to hand over
  • Plan before building. Each flow's triggers, actions, conditions and error paths were documented before any tool was touched.
  • Duplicate checks first. Workflows look for an existing contact or record before creating a new one.
  • AI with guardrails. The AI agent returns structured output, its decisions are logged in the sheet, and anything uncertain is flagged for a person to review.
  • Traceable. Every booking change, call outcome and AI result is logged in Google Sheets or the CRM.
  • Documented. A walkthrough and written notes let the agency's team own and maintain it.

Zapier: Booking, Onboarding & Follow-Up Automations

Seven Zapier workflows that take the repeat admin out of bookings, client intake, onboarding and team updates. Each one starts from a booking, a form response, an email or a task and finishes the job without anyone copying details between apps.

ZapierNotionGoogle SheetsAirtableSlack
35hrs
saved every month across the five workflow groups below
94%
less hands-on time on these tasks
426hrs
saved a year at these sample volumes
7zaps
built, each with its own error handling and filters

Estimates, not measured client data. These are portfolio builds, so the monthly volumes beside each row are sample numbers. Manual times are typical handling per event for a VA or admin; the automated figure is the review time that remains.

01 The problem

Every booking, form response, client email and new task needed someone to copy details between apps, send the right message and remember the follow-up. Steps were missed, replies went out late, and records drifted out of date.

02 The build

Each trigger, such as a Calendly booking, a Google Form response, an inbound email or a new Notion task, starts a Zap that filters, formats and routes the data. Paths split by free or paid, by priority or by status, and AI reads inbound emails.

03 The result

Every event is logged in Notion, Sheets or Airtable, the right email or alert goes out on time, and the team steps in only when a person is really needed.
